newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Down despite firm fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Down despite firm fundamentals.

text.p: Light ends edged down with crude and aggressive selling of gasoline despite of bullish fundamentals, traders said on Friday.
"People are offering down the market," said a trader on the gasoline market. "Physical wise, it is quite tight on the prompt."
All three gasoline grades lifting in March were offered lower intraday with only one bid seen.
Unleaded 95-octane was offered down 40 cents per barrel to $26.80 per barrel fob Singapore, while 97-octane's offer was lowered by 70 cents to $27.10.
A Japanese trader's offer for 92-octane was lowered to $26.30 from $26.60. On Thursday, a cargo of the same grade was traded at $26.40. Another Japanese trader's bid was only at $25.80.
Naphtha fell with crude as the Singapore market lacked trader direction amid Kuwaiti term talks with Asian buyers for March 1997-February 1998 supplies.
The latest indications were around $13-$14 over Mideast quotes. Term cargoes lifting August 1996-September 1997 were concluded at a $7.90 premium, traders said.
March naphtha swaps fell by 20-25 cents per barrel to $23.80/$24.00 per barrel.
